newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Attorney declines comment on ConAgra.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Attorney declines comment on ConAgra.

text.p: The U.S. Attorney for the southern district of Indiana declined to comment on a Wall Street Journal story that said ConAgra had agreed to pay millions of dollars in penalties to settle a criminal investigation into allegations of grain adulteration.
The attorney, Judith Stewart, told Reuters in a telephone interview from her office in Indianapolis that she could not even confirm that a criminal investigation of ConAgra was under way.
"I can state that there has been nothing public filed by this office -- no charges, no agreement, no nothing," Stewart said.
"I have no comment beyond saying there has been nothing public filed," Stewart said. She declined to comment on whether the U.S. Department of Justice had reached an agreement with ConAgra.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that the Justice Department had planned to announce details of ConAgra's penalties at a news conference Thursday in Indianapolis, but that the conference was scuttled amid hitches over the wording of the agreement.
Stewart said her office had not scheduled a news conference for Thursday.
"There is no news conference scheduled at all at this point," Stewart said.
A ConAgra spokeswoman also declined to comment on the story earlier Thursday.
